explanation: The best-known haka, 'Ka Mate', was composed around 1820 by Te Rauparaha, a Ngāti Toa chief. Samoa, Tonga and Fiji have their own war dances: the siva tau, sipi tau and cibi.

claims.text: The haka is a ceremonial dance of the Māori people of New Zealand.
The haka does not come from Samoan, Fijian or Tongan tradition.
'Ka Mate', the best-known haka, was composed around 1820 by Te Rauparaha, a chief of Ngāti Toa.
Samoa's siva tau, Tonga's sipi tau and Fiji's cibi are their own war dances, performed by their rugby teams.
